independent_review.summary: Approved as a bounded source review of the exact V2 artifact. Both prior findings are addressed: registration receipt replay now requires the current checkout, workspace, Git identity, state path and state inode; ProjectHost activation compares the supplied context's actual manager workspace and resolved state root against the registered manager before mounting. Thus restoring old root A after recovery to B cannot use the old startup receipt or mount an A context with B metadata. Persisted recovery receipts now validate paths lexically, independently of filesystem changes, while public availability retains canonical-path and directory-identity checks; a recovered root or ancestor becoming a symlink makes that binding unavailable without invalidating unrelated projects. Recovery retains locking, revision checks, existing-root ownership and snapshot validation, stable project identity and historical receipts. The CLI read-only guard and read-only listing are consistent, project is registered in the CLI and included in its command inventory, and hosted child applications receive the real host port. Inspected regression source covers restored old-root replay, mismatched supplied context, direct/ancestor symlink readability, unrelated-project availability, mounted-context refusal after recovery, recovery CAS/idempotency and CLI guards. No additional blocking defect found in inspected source. No canonical verifications were available; I did not execute tests, make check, visual checks or live Blizhe recovery, and this approval does not claim task completion. Artifact output was large and reader-redacted; bounded source reads supplemented it, with exact hash matches for the two regression test files. Authentication setup lines and a test email remained redacted; no absence claim depends on them.
